notes: Re-ran both AUD-0045 probes byte-for-byte and got identical output, so the raw measurements are reproducible. But the headline claim ('5 fail-open execution cases') does not survive falsification: I manually re-executed each of the 5 labeled 'fail_open=True' cases and read their source. (1) unitgate.py no-args is NOT a corner-case input -- it is the tool's default production invocation, and its main() explicitly fails closed on a collapsed read (`if report['units_scanned'] < MIN_UNITS: return 1`, `if report['artifacts_seen'] < MIN_ARTIFACTS: return 1`) before ever printing a success line; it printed real measured counts (units=2007, artifacts=326, vacuous-declarations=3) on this run. This is a confirmed false positive: the probe's classifier regex only recognizes the words items/violations/files/gates/checks/paths/errors/findings plus a few key=value idioms, and 'units=' / 'artifacts=' aren't in that list, so a gate that measured and fail-closed correctly was mislabeled fail-open. (2) rail_count_gate.py --self-test, (3) claim_gate.py --self-test, and (4) check_citations.py --self-test are not gate invocations on empty/absent production input at all -- their own docstrings/CLI define --self-test as a 'DETECTOR CONTROL' that runs every check against a KNOWN-BROKEN fixture and requires it to fire (rail_count_gate.py line 67: 'DETECTOR CONTROL. --self-test runs every check against a KNOWN-BROKEN input and requires it to [fire]'; claim_gate.py has a dedicated self_test() function; check_citations.py's own doc says '--self-test mutates each citation's expected value and asserts the checker goes RED'). Each of these printed a real measured count on this run (rail_count_gate: '50 cases, 27 of them expecting a FIRE'; claim_gate: '11 rules fire in the known-broken state'; check_citations: 'mutated 259 citations ... every citation went RED') that the same narrow regex failed to recognize. Conflating a self-test/detector-control invocation with a production gate call, and then further mis-scoring it via a regex with a small vocabulary, produced 3 more false positives. (5) ssot_drift_gate.py default is the one case that holds up: it exits 0 and its own text says 'this run asserted NOTHING about whether the live fleet is executing stale bytes' because the executed checkout path it checks against is a Windows path absent on this Linux runner -- a genuine confirmed fail-open exit. Net result: of the 5 claimed fail-open cases, only 1 (ssot_drift_gate.py) is a real fail-open finding; the other 4 are classifier/methodology artifacts, not defects in the underlying gates. The headline count is overstated by 5x (1 real vs. 5 claimed), so I could not confirm the report's headline as written and am returning FAIL. The AUD-0045-D-FAIL-OPEN defect should be narrowed to ssot_drift_gate.py only, and the probe2 classifier's has_measured_count() regex should be revised (or self-test/--self-test invocations excluded from the fail-open tally entirely) before this unit can be marked reviewed/PASS. I did not edit the receipt, probes, or defect records, and made no commits.
